reference.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students / Snell's Clinical Anatomy
clinicalPearls: Pyramidal bony cavity formed by seven bones: frontal, sphenoid, ethmoid, lacrimal, maxilla, zygomatic and palatine
Lateral rectus is innervated by CN VI (abducens); superior oblique by CN IV (trochlear); all other extraocular muscles by CN III (oculomotor)
Superior oblique passes through the fibrocartilaginous trochlea and depresses the adducted eye; inferior oblique elevates the adducted eye
Ciliary ganglion receives preganglionic parasympathetics from CN III and supplies sphincter pupillae (constriction) and ciliary muscle (accommodation)
Superior orbital fissure syndrome impairs CN III, IV, V1 and VI, causing ophthalmoplegia and forehead sensory loss
reference.pathophysiology: The orbit encloses the globe, extraocular muscles, orbital fat and neurovascular structures. The common tendinous ring of Zinn encircles the optic canal and central superior orbital fissure. Pathologies including orbital cellulitis, thyroid eye disease (Graves orbitopathy) with extraocular muscle belly enlargement sparing tendons, and orbital apex syndrome produce proptosis, diplopia and visual loss.
additionalInvestigations: High-resolution orbital CT without contrast for fractures
Contrast-enhanced orbital MRI with fat suppression for optic nerve lesions
Hess screen / Lancaster red-green test for diplopia quantification
